goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs — `{{#unless automatic}}` is evaluated in the per-member item view context instead of the group context, so the remove link will likely render for automatic groups (or always be hidden), defeating the guard

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs`, members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, which uses the `group-member` item view (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`). The item view does not define/proxy an `automatic` property. In `admin/templates/group_member.hbs`, the guard `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}` will therefore resolve `automatic` in the item-view (or member) context, where it’s likely `undefined`/falsey, causing the remove link to render even for automatic groups (or otherwise not respect the group’s `automatic` flag).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb (add_members) — non-existent usernames silently skipped with no error reporting; response returns success even if no usernames matched, indistinguishable from a successful add

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; otherwise it does nothing. It then calls `group.save` and returns `success_json` on save success, even if zero usernames matched and no users were added. That makes “no-op because all usernames were invalid” indistinguishable from “members added”, but the diff does not establish that this is incorrect behavior (prior code also silently ignored non-existent users), so it’s more an API/UX/feedback concern than a verifiable defect.

For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 adds an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and suggests Math.ceil as the fix, matching the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb (remove_member) — `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save` bypasses `Group#remove`, so denormalized `user_count` may not be decremented; test only checks association count, not `user_count`

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` is used instead of the previously-used domain method pattern (`group.add(user)` / `group.remove(user)` in the old controller logic and still in `add_members`). This inconsistency could bypass any side effects/callbacks that `Group#remove` might perform (e.g., maintaining a cached/denormalized `user_count`), and the new spec only asserts `group.users.count` rather than any counter field. However, the diff does not show the `Group#remove` implementation or whether `user_count` is denormalized/counter-cached, so the concrete defect cannot be verified solely from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb (add_members) — usernames split on `,` only with no whitespace stripping; `"alice, bob"` fails to find ` bob` and silently skips that user

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` followed by `User.find_by_username(username)` with no `strip`/whitespace normalization. This means input like `"alice, bob"` produces a username token `" bob"`, which will not match and will be silently skipped (the code only adds if a user is found). This is a real behavior defect in the added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb (add_members) — no cap on number of usernames per request; arbitrarily large list causes N queries + `group.add` calls in a transaction-free loop (potential DoS / partial-failure state with no rollback)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each` and a per-username `User.find_by_username` + `group.add(user)` loop, with no limit on input size and no transaction/rollback. This makes the endpoint vulnerable to very large requests causing many DB queries and repeated membership mutations, and if an exception occurs mid-loop it can leave the group partially modified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 (next/previous) — `offset` set on the model before `findMembers()`; if the AJAX request fails, offset points at the new page while members shows old data, desyncing the pager

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` actions `next`/`previous`, the code sets `group.set("offset", offset)` before calling `group.findMembers()`. `findMembers()` updates `members`/`offset` only in the AJAX `.then(...)` (success path) and there is no failure handling. If the request fails, `offset` (and thus `currentPage`/`showingFirst`/`showingLast`) reflects the new page while `members` remains the old list, causing pager/UI state to desync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb — no test for paginated `GroupsController#members` endpoint (limit/offset/meta.total) despite response format changing from flat array to `{members: ..., meta: ...}`

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public `GroupsController#members` response from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a flat array) to a JSON object with `members:` and `meta: { total, limit, offset }`, and adds pagination params (`limit`, `offset`) in `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`. No corresponding test is added in this diff to assert the new shape/pagination/meta behavior. While the finding points at `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` (which wouldn’t be the natural place to test `GroupsController`), the underlying issue—missing test coverage for the changed endpoint—is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb (members) — response shape changed from serialized array to `{members: ..., meta: {...}}` with no version note, breaking existing API consumers; also uses raw `render json:` with `serialize_data` instead of `render_serialized`, bypassing error/JSON conventions

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, which is a breaking response-shape change for any clients expecting an array. It also replaces the conventional `render_serialized` path with a raw `render json:` + `serialize_data` payload. This is a real, diff-grounded compatibility/architecture concern, but not a provable runtime defect within the PR itself (the frontend was updated to consume `result.members`/`meta`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb (members) — an extra `group.users.count` query is always executed even when the caller can't use pagination metadata; count could be cached or omitted via a param

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new implementation always executes `total = group.users.count` and then separately fetches the paged `members` (`order...limit...offset`), which is an extra query on every request (diff shows this was introduced). Whether the caller “can’t use” the metadata is not supported by the diff (the JSON response now always includes `meta.total`, and the JS `findMembers()` consumes it), but the core performance concern about an unconditional count query is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 (addMembers) — `usernames` input is never cleared after adding (acknowledged TODO), so clicking 'Add' twice re-submits the same list and stale usernames accumulate

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and then calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without ever resetting `this.set("usernames", null/"")`. Since the template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, the entered usernames remain in the bound property, so clicking “Add” again will resubmit the same list (stale input persists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js (addMembers) — no error handling on the AJAX call; a 422 response (e.g. automatic group) leaves the promise rejection unhandled and the admin gets no UI feedback. Same for `removeMember`

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, both `addMembers` and `removeMember` only attach a `.then(...)` success handler and do not handle AJAX failures (no `.catch`/error callback). The controller actions also don’t return/await these promises (`addMembers` just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`; `removeMember` calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` inside the confirm callback), so a 4xx/5xx (including 422) would result in a rejected promise with no UI feedback. The specific “automatic group” 422 example is less likely from the admin UI because the template hides those controls with `{{#unless automatic}}`, but the silent failure/unhandled rejection issue is still real for other error cases.
